title: The platform
description: Is what the factory runs on healthy, and if not, what? Each worker’s memory, CPU and event loop against its limits; the store and Postgres; the telemetry pipeline; delivery through Argo CD, Argo Rollouts and Kyverno; and the workers’ logs.

list.name: Releases
list.textFormat: The line recorded a release’s end

list.name: service_name
list.label: Worker
list.description: The workers whose logs to read, or all of them

list.name: level
list.label: Level
list.description: Which of the workers’ log lines to show
list.query: everything : .*, warnings and errors : warn|error|critical|fatal, errors : error|critical|fatal

panels.title: Each worker now
panels.description: Every worker and the console: memory used of its limit (Kubernetes kills it at 100%), CPU used of what it requests, how late its event loop runs (p99), its heap, and over the range its restarts and the warnings and errors it logged. Good is green across. Select a worker to read its logs below.

targets.expr: max by (worker) (label_replace(max by (container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="factory", container!=""}) / max by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="factory", resource="memory"}), "worker", "$1", "container", "(.+)") and on (worker) label_replace(group by (job) (v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes{job=~"software-factory/.+"}), "worker", "$1", "job", "software-factory/(.+)"))

max by (worker) (label_replace(sum by (container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="factory", container!=""}[5m])) / max by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="factory", resource="cpu"}), "worker", "$1", "container", "(.+)") and on (worker) label_replace(group by (job) (v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes{job=~"software-factory/.+"}), "worker", "$1", "job", "software-factory/(.+)"))

max by (worker) (label_replace(sum by (container) (round(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="factory"}[$__range]))), "worker", "$1", "container", "(.+)") and on (worker) label_replace(group by (job) (v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes{job=~"software-factory/.+"}), "worker", "$1", "job", "software-factory/(.+)"))

panels.title: Memory, of each worker’s limit
panels.description: Each worker’s working memory as a share of its limit: at 100% Kubernetes kills it. A line that climbs and never falls is a leak. The dashed lines are 80% and 95%; the legend puts the highest first.

targets.expr: max by (worker) (label_replace(max by (container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="factory", container!=""}) / max by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="factory", resource="memory"}), "worker", "$1", "container", "(.+)") and on (worker) label_replace(group by (job) (v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes{job=~"software-factory/.+"}), "worker", "$1", "job", "software-factory/(.+)"))

panels.title: Event loop, p99 delay
panels.description: How late each worker’s event loop ran what was due, at its 99th percentile: a worker busy computing, or blocked, answers nothing meanwhile. About 10 ms is the timer’s own grain; the dashed lines are 100 ms and 1 s.

panels.title: Postgres
panels.description: Whether the exporter reached Postgres at its last scrape. Every worker’s state is there: down, the line and triage stop.

panels.title: Connections, of the maximum
panels.description: Connections Postgres holds now, every client’s together, as a share of its max_connections. Past it, a worker cannot connect. Good is under 70%.

panels.title: Queries failed
panels.description: Queries the workers’ store clients saw fail in the range, whatever the cause: a constraint, a conflict to retry, or a lost connection. The panel below names their codes. Good is none.

panels.title: Connections failed
panels.description: Connections a worker tried to open in the range that closed before they opened: refused, timed out, or ended as the worker stopped. A few at a deploy are expected; a steady count is Postgres out of reach.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks Postgres broke in the factory’s database in the range, rolling one side back. Good is none.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: The factory’s database on disk now: the event store, the inbox, the line and the artifacts’ index. It grows with the work done; a jump is worth a look.

panels.title: Query time, p95 by statement
panels.description: The 95th percentile of how long the workers’ queries took, by the statement’s first word, from asking to answer, so a wait for a free connection counts. A listen is left out: it holds its connection open for as long as the worker runs.

panels.title: Queries failed, by code
panels.description: Queries that failed, by their code: Postgres’s SQLSTATE (23505 a duplicate, 40001 a conflict to retry) or the client’s own (CONNECTION_CLOSED, ECONNREFUSED). Each bar is its interval’s count. Good is none.

defaults.noValue: No query failed in this range

panels.title: Connections, by worker
panels.description: The connections each worker’s store client holds open now, its listen included. Each holds a small pool; one far above the rest is leaking.

panels.title: Transactions, committed and rolled back
panels.description: Transactions a second in the factory’s database, by how they ended. A rollback is a conflict retried or a failure undone: a few are normal, many beside few commits are not.

panels.title: Dropped in the range
panels.description: Spans, metric points and log records lost in the range: refused or failed at the collectors, failed on the way out of them, or refused or discarded by Tempo and Loki. Good is none of each.

targets.expr: (sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_refused_spans[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_failed_spans[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(tempo_receiver_refused_spans[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(tempo_discarded_spans_total[$__range]))) or vector(0))

(sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_refused_metric_points[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_failed_metric_points[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_metric_points[$__range]))) or vector(0))

(sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_refused_log_records[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_receiver_failed_log_records[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_log_records[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(round(increase(loki_discarded_samples_total[$__range]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Export queues, how full
panels.description: How full each of the collectors’ queues to Tempo, Prometheus and Loki is now. A backend slow or down fills its queue; full, the collector drops what comes next. Good is near empty.

panels.title: Metrics kept
panels.description: How far back Prometheus’s oldest sample is. It keeps seven days, or less when its disk cap comes first; the error budget reads seven days, so with fewer kept it is over fewer. Good is six days or more.

panels.title: Storage, of its cap
panels.description: Prometheus’s blocks on disk as a share of its size cap. At the cap it deletes its oldest block, so the days kept beside it fall; near it is the usual state of a busy week.

panels.title: Series
panels.description: Series in Prometheus’s head block: the cost of every label. A step up is a new label with many values, which a dashboard should never need: work items are in traces and logs.

panels.title: Into the collectors, by signal
panels.description: What the collectors accepted a second, by signal: spans and metric points over OTLP, and log records over OTLP and from the pods’ log files. A signal falling to nothing is a sender gone quiet.

panels.title: Into Tempo and Loki
panels.description: What Tempo and Loki received a second: spans and log lines. Each should follow what the collectors accepted beside it; a gap that opens is telemetry lost between them.

defaults.noValue: Tempo and Loki are not reporting

panels.title: Argo CD’s applications
panels.description: Each application Argo CD keeps in step with main, over the range: synced and healthy, out of sync or still progressing (normal for a minute after a merge), or degraded or missing.

targets.expr: max by (name) (2 * argocd_app_info{health_status=~"Degraded|Missing"} or argocd_app_info{sync_status!="Synced"} or argocd_app_info{health_status!="Healthy"} or 0 * argocd_app_info)

panels.title: Argo CD’s syncs
panels.description: Syncs Argo CD ran, by how they ended. Each merge to main that changes an application is one or more; a failed sync leaves the cluster behind main. Each bar is its interval’s count.

panels.title: Argo Rollouts’ rollouts
panels.description: Each Rollout over the range: stable, a canary in progress, or a canary aborted, which Argo Rollouts does when its analysis fails. The app’s is the one the line releases.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (rollout_phase{phase=~"Progressing|Paused"}) + 2 * max by (namespace, name) (rollout_phase{phase=~"Abort|Error|Timeout"})

panels.title: Admissions, allowed and denied
panels.description: Requests Kyverno’s admission control judged, by its answer. A denial is an image not signed on main, or something else its policies forbid, kept out of the cluster. Each bar is its interval’s count.

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: Lines the workers chosen above logged at warn, error or worse, by level. A few warnings are routine (a sense that could not tell); an error is worth reading below. Each bar is its interval’s count.

defaults.noValue: No warnings or errors in this range

panels.title: The workers’ logs
panels.description: What the factory’s workers said, newest first, for the workers and level chosen above. A line with a trace opens it.
